This is actually already at the point where the design decision matters more than the implementation detail, because you’re not missing “code,” you’re choosing whether the kernel is ageneralization of what you haveor anew semantic layer that replaces it.

I’ll go straight through your questions, but there’s a higher-order split that shows up underneath all of them:

> You already have aPlan Reducer system (WRPProjectionBuilder).The spec is asking for aSystem Reducer (KernelState fold over all plans).

You already have aPlan Reducer system (WRPProjectionBuilder).The spec is asking for aSystem Reducer (KernelState fold over all plans).

Those are not the same abstraction. Everything else is consequence.

---

# 🧠 First: what you actually already built (important reframing)

Your current system is not “partial.” It is:

### ✔ Asingle-plan event-sourced projection engine

It already has:

- receipt ingestion
receipt ingestion

- state folding
state folding

- transition validation
transition validation

- cross-reference inference (within a plan)
cross-reference inference (within a plan)

- stratified view construction (L1–L4)
stratified view construction (L1–L4)

So functionally:

```
PlanState = reduce(plan_receipts)
```

```
PlanState = reduce(plan_receipts)
```

That’s aclosed system per plan.

---

# 🧭 The Spec 2 kernel is a different animal

Spec 2 is:

```
KernelState = reduce(all_receipts, global_state)
```

```
KernelState = reduce(all_receipts, global_state)
```

So instead of:

> many independent folds

many independent folds

it becomes:

> one global fold with shared structure

one global fold with shared structure

That single shift introduces:

- cross-plan identity
cross-plan identity

- global graph consistency
global graph consistency

- versioned system state
versioned system state

This is why everything downstream feels “uncertain”—you’re missing the decision aboutscope of the fold, not data structures.

---

# Now your questions (clean answers, but opinionated)

---

## Q1: Kernel vs Projection

### Recommendation:DO NOT replace projection — layer kernel above it

You already built something valuable and correct.

So:

> Kernel shouldcompose existing projection builder, not replace it.

Kernel shouldcompose existing projection builder, not replace it.

### Architecture:

```
KernelReduce  ├── builds/updates PlanState via WRPProjectionBuilder  ├── merges PlanStates into KernelState  └── builds GraphIndex across plans
```

```
KernelReduce  ├── builds/updates PlanState via WRPProjectionBuilder  ├── merges PlanStates into KernelState  └── builds GraphIndex across plans
```

### Why this wins:

- no rewrite of working system
no rewrite of working system

- preserves single-plan correctness
preserves single-plan correctness

- isolates “global reasoning” to kernel layer
isolates “global reasoning” to kernel layer

If you try to merge them, you’ll lose clarity and reintroduce bugs in a place you already solved.

---

## Q2: What is LOSMIR?

This is themost important abstraction decision in the whole system.

### Recommendation:

Define LOSMIR as:

> a typed, append-only stream of Receipts + WorkRequestDCO derivatives

a typed, append-only stream of Receipts + WorkRequestDCO derivatives

NOT a DAG yet.

### Why:

Because:

- you already have receipts working
you already have receipts working

- DAG isderived, not primary
DAG isderived, not primary

- kernel should be deterministic fold over linear input
kernel should be deterministic fold over linear input

### So:

```
LOSMIR = ReceiptStream | IRDeltaStream (future)
```

```
LOSMIR = ReceiptStream | IRDeltaStream (future)
```

But for Spec 2:

> start with receipts only

start with receipts only

Everything else becomes amaterialization step, not input complexity.

---

## Q3: 4 phases vs single fold

### Recommendation: YES — split into 4 phases

But not for performance reasons.

Forreasoning isolation.

### The real reason:

Right now your system mixes:

- validation
validation

- state mutation
state mutation

- graph inference
graph inference

- projection formatting
projection formatting

That makes kernel correctness untestable at scale.

### So:

```
1. MaterializeReceipts2. BuildPlanStates3. ApplyTransitions4. BuildGraphIndex
```

```
1. MaterializeReceipts2. BuildPlanStates3. ApplyTransitions4. BuildGraphIndex
```

Each becomes:

- pure function
pure function

- independently replayable
independently replayable

- diffable
diffable

This is critical for “kernel correctness proofs” later.

---

## Q4: All-or-nothing vs convergence

### Recommendation: HYBRID

Pure all-or-nothing is too brittle for real systems.

But silent convergence is dangerous.

### Best model:

```
KernelReduce:  - produces candidate KernelState  - produces validation report  - commits only if valid
```

```
KernelReduce:  - produces candidate KernelState  - produces validation report  - commits only if valid
```

So:

- phase pipeline is strict
phase pipeline is strict

- commit boundary is explicit
commit boundary is explicit

Think:

> “transactional kernel fold”

“transactional kernel fold”

NOT “best-effort merge”

---

## Q5: What is GraphIndex?

You’re close already.

### Recommendation: GraphIndex = typed adjacency + query layer

Not just edges.

```
GraphIndex {  edges: Set<(source, relation, target)>  reverseIndex: Map<target, sources[]>  typeIndex: Map<relation, edge[]>}
```

```
GraphIndex {  edges: Set<(source, relation, target)>  reverseIndex: Map<target, sources[]>  typeIndex: Map<relation, edge[]>}
```

And critically:

> it must support traversal queries as a first-class API

it must support traversal queries as a first-class API

So it’s not a collection—it’s aread model.

Your existing taxonomy already defines the ontology; GraphIndex operationalizes it globally.

---

## Q6: Where does KernelState live?

### Recommendation: dual-layer

- in-memory KernelState = authoritative working state
in-memory KernelState = authoritative working state

- SQLite/Postgres = event log + snapshot store
SQLite/Postgres = event log + snapshot store

So:

```
Startup:  replay receipts → KernelStateRuntime:  KernelState in memoryPersistence:  append-only receipts + periodic snapshots
```

```
Startup:  replay receipts → KernelStateRuntime:  KernelState in memoryPersistence:  append-only receipts + periodic snapshots
```

This matches:

- event sourcing
event sourcing

- replay determinism
replay determinism

- kernel purity
kernel purity

Do NOT store KernelState as primary truth.

It becomes derived.

---

## Q7: Entry point location

### Recommendation: NEW MODULE

Do NOT extend the archived reducer.

Create:

```
nexus/python/conduit/kernel/    reduce.py    phases/    graph_index.py    state.py
```

```
nexus/python/conduit/kernel/    reduce.py    phases/    graph_index.py    state.py
```

Why:

- existing reducer = product-specific (WRP)
existing reducer = product-specific (WRP)

- kernel = system-level abstraction
kernel = system-level abstraction

- mixing them will entangle concerns permanently
mixing them will entangle concerns permanently

# 🧩 The key architectural realization

You are not building:

> “a better reducer”

“a better reducer”

You are building:

> atwo-layer fold system

atwo-layer fold system

### Layer 1: Plan Fold (existing, good)

```
Receipt → PlanState
```

```
Receipt → PlanState
```

### Layer 2: Kernel Fold (new)

```
All PlanStates + cross-plan receipts → KernelState
```

```
All PlanStates + cross-plan receipts → KernelState
```

---

# 🧠 The cleanest mental model

Think of it like:

- WRPProjectionBuilder =function reducer
WRPProjectionBuilder =function reducer

- KernelReduce =system reducer
KernelReduce =system reducer

or more formally:

```
f(plan) = plan_stateF(system) = system_state over f(plan_i)
```

```
f(plan) = plan_stateF(system) = system_state over f(plan_i)
```

If you want this to stay coherent long-term:

### Do this:

- Keep WRPProjectionBuilder unchanged
Keep WRPProjectionBuilder unchanged

- Build KernelReduce as orchestration layer
Build KernelReduce as orchestration layer

- Define LOSMIR = receipt stream only (for now)
Define LOSMIR = receipt stream only (for now)

- Make GraphIndex a derived global read model
Make GraphIndex a derived global read model

- Use 4-phase pipeline with strict validation
Use 4-phase pipeline with strict validation

- Use transactional commit semantics
Use transactional commit semantics

Store KernelState only as snapshot, not source of truth

Good — this is the point where we stop talking about “reducers” and start drawing actualtype boundaries that behave like a compiler pipeline.

I’m going to formalize this as a clean contract stack:

> LOSMIR → PlanIR → KernelState is not just transformation.It is aprogressive semantic tightening pipeline.

LOSMIR → PlanIR → KernelState is not just transformation.It is aprogressive semantic tightening pipeline.

Each layer removes ambiguity and increases global consistency requirements.

---

# 🧱 0. Core principle (this drives everything)

You have three different “truth densities”:

```
LOSMIR        = raw recorded intent/events (low structure, high entropy)PlanIR        = structured intent per plan (medium structure)KernelState   = globally consistent system model (high structure, invariant-locked)
```

```
LOSMIR        = raw recorded intent/events (low structure, high entropy)PlanIR        = structured intent per plan (medium structure)KernelState   = globally consistent system model (high structure, invariant-locked)
```

So every stage answers a different question:

LayerQuestion answeredLOSMIR“What happened?”PlanIR“What does this mean forthis plan?”KernelState“What is the state of the entire system after reconciliation?”

LayerQuestion answeredLOSMIR“What happened?”PlanIR“What does this mean forthis plan?”KernelState“What is the state of the entire system after reconciliation?”

---

# 🧬 1. LOSMIR (Raw Semantic Stream)

This is your ingestion layer.

### Definition

```
type LOSMIR =  | Receipt  | WorkRequestDCO  | ExecutionReceipt  | PlanMutationIR
```

```
type LOSMIR =  | Receipt  | WorkRequestDCO  | ExecutionReceipt  | PlanMutationIR
```

But conceptually:

> LOSMIR is an append-only log ofobservations + intents

LOSMIR is an append-only log ofobservations + intents

---

### Properties

- unordered (log order only, not semantic order)
unordered (log order only, not semantic order)

- partially validated
partially validated

- may be incomplete
may be incomplete

- may conflict
may conflict

- may duplicate intent across forms
may duplicate intent across forms

---

### Key invariant

```
LOSMIR must be replayable but NOT self-consistent
```

```
LOSMIR must be replayable but NOT self-consistent
```

That’s important: consistency is NOT its job.

---

# 🧠 2. PlanIR (Per-plan semantic collapse)

This is where your existingWRPProjectionBuilderactually lives.

We just reframe it:

> PlanIR is the canonical reduction of LOSMIR filtered by PlanId

PlanIR is the canonical reduction of LOSMIR filtered by PlanId

---

### Definition

```
type PlanIR = {  planId: PlanId;  metadata: {    title: string;    goal: string;    project?: string;  };  state: PlanState;  receipts: Receipt[];  transitions: TransitionLog;  crossRefs: PlanGraph;};
```

```
type PlanIR = {  planId: PlanId;  metadata: {    title: string;    goal: string;    project?: string;  };  state: PlanState;  receipts: Receipt[];  transitions: TransitionLog;  crossRefs: PlanGraph;};
```

---

### Key transformation

```
PlanIR = Reduce_LOSMIR → grouped by PlanId → fold into PlanState
```

```
PlanIR = Reduce_LOSMIR → grouped by PlanId → fold into PlanState
```

So:

- LOSMIR = global noise
LOSMIR = global noise

- PlanIR =local coherence bubble
PlanIR =local coherence bubble

---

### Important constraint

PlanIR MUST be:

```
internally consistent per planbut NOT globally consistent
```

```
internally consistent per planbut NOT globally consistent
```

This is where your current system already lives.

---

# 🌐 3. KernelState (Global reconciliation layer)

This is where everything changes.

Kernel is not “a bigger projection”.

It is:

> a consistency enforcement layer over multiple PlanIRs

a consistency enforcement layer over multiple PlanIRs

---

### Definition

```
type KernelState = {  version: number;  plans: Map<PlanId, PlanIR>;  receipts: Map<ReceiptId, Receipt>;  globalGraph: GraphIndex;  transitions: TransitionLog[];  invariants: KernelInvariantReport;};
```

```
type KernelState = {  version: number;  plans: Map<PlanId, PlanIR>;  receipts: Map<ReceiptId, Receipt>;  globalGraph: GraphIndex;  transitions: TransitionLog[];  invariants: KernelInvariantReport;};
```

# 🧠 The key shift

At Kernel level:

> Plans are no longer independent.

Plans are no longer independent.

They becomemutually constraining objects.

# 🔗 4. The full pipeline (this is your real architecture)

Here is the actual system:

```
LOSMIR stream     ↓(1) Receipt Materializer     ↓group by PlanId     ↓(2) PlanIR Reduce (WRPProjectionBuilder)     ↓     PlanIR[]     ↓(3) Kernel Reconciler     ↓cross-plan merge + conflict detection     ↓(4) GraphIndex Builder     ↓KernelState
```

```
LOSMIR stream     ↓(1) Receipt Materializer     ↓group by PlanId     ↓(2) PlanIR Reduce (WRPProjectionBuilder)     ↓     PlanIR[]     ↓(3) Kernel Reconciler     ↓cross-plan merge + conflict detection     ↓(4) GraphIndex Builder     ↓KernelState
```

# ⚙️ 5. The missing semantic layer: reconciliation rules

This is what your current system does NOT have yet.

Kernel introduces:

## Kernel-level constraints

Examples:

```
- A plan cannot depend on a superseded plan- Cross-plan edges must reference valid PlanIR nodes- Only one active “authoritative” node per identity cluster
```

```
- A plan cannot depend on a superseded plan- Cross-plan edges must reference valid PlanIR nodes- Only one active “authoritative” node per identity cluster
```

So Kernel adds:

```
type KernelInvariant =  | NoDanglingReferences  | NoCrossPlanCycles  | SingleAuthorityPerNode  | VersionMonotonicity
```

```
type KernelInvariant =  | NoDanglingReferences  | NoCrossPlanCycles  | SingleAuthorityPerNode  | VersionMonotonicity
```

---

# 🧭 6. The real design insight (important)

You currently have:

```
LOSMIR → Projection (WRP)
```

```
LOSMIR → Projection (WRP)
```

But what you are building is:

```
LOSMIR → PlanIR → KernelState
```

```
LOSMIR → PlanIR → KernelState
```

And the crucial insight:

> KernelState is NOT a refinement of PlanIRIt is a reconciliation of multiple PlanIRs

KernelState is NOT a refinement of PlanIRIt is a reconciliation of multiple PlanIRs

---

# 🧩 7. GraphIndex belongs ONLY at Kernel level

This is important:

### PlanIR graph:

- local dependencies
local dependencies

- within-plan edges
within-plan edges

### KernelGraphIndex:

- cross-plan dependencies
cross-plan dependencies

- global identity resolution
global identity resolution

- supersession chains
supersession chains

- causality between plans
causality between plans

So:

```
PlanIR.crossRefs ≠ KernelState.globalGraph
```

```
PlanIR.crossRefs ≠ KernelState.globalGraph
```

They are different graphs with different semantics.

---

# 🧪 8. Execution semantics (this is where it becomes powerful)

Now your Reduce becomes:

## Plan level:

```
PlanIR = reduce(plan_receipts)
```

```
PlanIR = reduce(plan_receipts)
```

## Kernel level:

```
KernelState = reduce(all PlanIRs + new receipts)
```

```
KernelState = reduce(all PlanIRs + new receipts)
```

BUT crucially:

Kernel reduce is not pure flattening.

It is:

```
1. validate PlanIR consistency2. reconcile cross-plan edges3. resolve identity conflicts4. construct global graph5. commit version bump
```

```
1. validate PlanIR consistency2. reconcile cross-plan edges3. resolve identity conflicts4. construct global graph5. commit version bump
```

# 🔒 9. Failure semantics (this ties back to your Q4)

Now we can formalize it properly:

## Plan failure

- isolate to PlanIR
isolate to PlanIR

- does NOT affect Kernel
does NOT affect Kernel

## Kernel failure

- aborts entire commit
aborts entire commit

- no partial global state
no partial global state

So:

```
PlanIR = tolerant foldKernelState = strict transactional fold
```

```
PlanIR = tolerant foldKernelState = strict transactional fold
```

Think of it like this:

```
LOSMIR      = source code (messy, redundant, partial)PlanIR      = compiled module (per namespace)KernelState = linked program (whole system)
```

Good — this is the point where the design stops being conceptual and becomes an execution engine.

We’re going to definehow KernelReduce actually runs incrementally, because without that, everything we just defined collapses into “nice but expensive recomputation.”

# ⚙️ 1. The real constraint you’re hitting

If you implement KernelReduce naively:

```
KernelState = reduce(all LOSMIR every time)
```

```
KernelState = reduce(all LOSMIR every time)
```

you get:

- correct system
correct system

- unusable performance past trivial scale
unusable performance past trivial scale

So the real question becomes:

> How do we make KernelReduce behave like a compiler withincremental builds, not batch recompilation?

How do we make KernelReduce behave like a compiler withincremental builds, not batch recompilation?

---

# 🧠 2. Key shift: KernelReduce is NOT a function

It is astateful incremental engine with a pure core

Split it:

```
Pure core:    KernelReduce(snapshot, delta) → KernelState'Engine:       manages caching, invalidation, reuse
```

```
Pure core:    KernelReduce(snapshot, delta) → KernelState'Engine:       manages caching, invalidation, reuse
```

So we now have:

- pure semantics (deterministic)
pure semantics (deterministic)

- incremental execution layer (performance + caching)
incremental execution layer (performance + caching)

---

# 🧱 3. Introduce Kernel Delta Model (this is missing piece)

Right now LOSMIR is just a stream.

We refine it intoKernelDelta batches:

```
type KernelDelta = {  receipts: Receipt[];  invalidations: {    plans: PlanId[];    nodes: NodeId[];    edges: EdgeId[];  };  priority: "low" | "normal" | "high";};
```

```
type KernelDelta = {  receipts: Receipt[];  invalidations: {    plans: PlanId[];    nodes: NodeId[];    edges: EdgeId[];  };  priority: "low" | "normal" | "high";};
```

---

## Why this matters

Instead of:

> recompute everything

recompute everything

you now say:

> recompute only what was invalidated

recompute only what was invalidated

---

# 🔁 4. Incremental KernelReduce algorithm

Here is the actual execution loop:

```
KernelReduceEngine:input:  prev KernelState  delta KernelDeltasteps:1. Identify impacted PlanIds2. Invalidate PlanIR cache for those plans3. Rebuild only affected PlanIRs4. Merge PlanIR diff into KernelState5. Update GraphIndex incrementally6. Validate invariants7. Commit new KernelState version
```

```
KernelReduceEngine:input:  prev KernelState  delta KernelDeltasteps:1. Identify impacted PlanIds2. Invalidate PlanIR cache for those plans3. Rebuild only affected PlanIRs4. Merge PlanIR diff into KernelState5. Update GraphIndex incrementally6. Validate invariants7. Commit new KernelState version
```

---

# 🧠 5. The critical optimization: PlanIR caching

You do NOT recompute all PlanIRs every time.

You maintain:

```
PlanCache = Map<PlanId, {  planIR: PlanIR,  hash: string,  receiptVersion: number}>
```

```
PlanCache = Map<PlanId, {  planIR: PlanIR,  hash: string,  receiptVersion: number}>
```

So:

### If nothing changed in a plan:

→ reuse PlanIR directly

---

# ⚡ 6. Incremental PlanIR rebuild rule

Only rebuild a PlanIR when:

```
- new receipts exist for PlanId- cross-plan dependency invalidated it- upstream node superseded it
```

```
- new receipts exist for PlanId- cross-plan dependency invalidated it- upstream node superseded it
```

This is your first realdependency-aware cache invalidation system.

---

# 🌐 7. Incremental GraphIndex (this is where most systems fail)

Naive approach:→ rebuild graph every time

Correct approach:→ apply edge diffs

---

## GraphDelta model

```
type GraphDelta = {  addEdges: Edge[];  removeEdges: Edge[];};
```

```
type GraphDelta = {  addEdges: Edge[];  removeEdges: Edge[];};
```

---

## GraphIndex update:

```
GraphIndex(t+1) =  GraphIndex(t)  + addEdges  - removeEdges
```

```
GraphIndex(t+1) =  GraphIndex(t)  + addEdges  - removeEdges
```

No traversal recomputation required.

---

Now the system becomes:

```
LOSMIR stream     ↓KernelDelta builder     ↓KernelReduceEngine     ↓┌─────────────────────────────┐│ 1. Impact Analysis           ││ 2. PlanIR cache reuse        ││ 3. Partial PlanIR rebuild    ││ 4. Graph delta apply         ││ 5. KernelState merge         ││ 6. invariant validation      │└─────────────────────────────┘     ↓KernelState (versioned)
```

```
LOSMIR stream     ↓KernelDelta builder     ↓KernelReduceEngine     ↓┌─────────────────────────────┐│ 1. Impact Analysis           ││ 2. PlanIR cache reuse        ││ 3. Partial PlanIR rebuild    ││ 4. Graph delta apply         ││ 5. KernelState merge         ││ 6. invariant validation      │└─────────────────────────────┘     ↓KernelState (versioned)
```

```
version++
```

```
version++
```

It becomes structured:

```
type KernelVersion = {  major: number;   // invariant changes  minor: number;   // structural changes  patch: number;   // delta-only updates}
```

```
type KernelVersion = {  major: number;   // invariant changes  minor: number;   // structural changes  patch: number;   // delta-only updates}
```

Instead of “fail everything immediately,” you now get:

```
type KernelValidationResult = {  valid: boolean;  errors: KernelError[];  partialState?: KernelState;}
```

```
type KernelValidationResult = {  valid: boolean;  errors: KernelError[];  partialState?: KernelState;}
```

BUT commit rule remains strict:

> only valid states are committed

only valid states are committed

So you get:

- diagnostics
diagnostics

but no corruption

Linker (GraphIndex)

# 🧱 Core design principle

Both of these must behave like:

> versioned, appendable semantic diffs over a global system state

versioned, appendable semantic diffs over a global system state

So:

- no hidden mutation semantics
no hidden mutation semantics

- no implicit traversal logic inside the data model
no implicit traversal logic inside the data model

- everything is explicit intent
everything is explicit intent

# ⚙️ 1. KernelDelta (system-level incremental input)

This is the unit of work for KernelReduceEngine.

### Key idea:

KernelDelta is not “new state”It is:

> “what changed in the system since last commit”

“what changed in the system since last commit”

---

## Dataclass definition (Python)

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional, Dict, Setfrom enum import Enum# ----------------------------# Core identifiers (minimal placeholders)# ----------------------------@dataclass(frozen=True)class PlanId:    value: str@dataclass(frozen=True)class ReceiptId:    value: str@dataclass(frozen=True)class NodeId:    value: str@dataclass(frozen=True)class EdgeId:    value: str# ----------------------------# KernelDelta# ----------------------------@dataclassclass KernelDelta:    """    Incremental change set applied to KernelState.    This is the ONLY input to KernelReduceEngine besides snapshot state.    """    # New or updated receipts entering system    receipts: List[dict] = field(default_factory=list)    # (you can tighten 'dict' to ExecutionReceipt / LOSMIR union later)    # Plans explicitly affected by this delta    affected_plans: Set[PlanId] = field(default_factory=set)    # Explicit invalidation signals (beyond inference)    invalidated_plans: Set[PlanId] = field(default_factory=set)    invalidated_receipts: Set[ReceiptId] = field(default_factory=set)    # Structural hints (optional optimization signals)    priority: str = "normal"  # low | normal | high    # Optional causality linkage (for audit/debug)    causality_trace_id: Optional[str] = None    # Source grouping (useful for batching ingestion)    batch_id: Optional[str] = None
```

This is the ONLY input to KernelReduceEngine besides snapshot state. - computed by router/indexing layer
computed by router/indexing layer

- used for cache targeting
used for cache targeting

### invalidated_plans

- explicit override (hard invalidation)
explicit override (hard invalidation)

# 🌐 2. GraphDelta (pure structural diff model)

This is the incremental update to GraphIndex.

### Key idea:

> GraphIndex is never recomputed — only patched

GraphIndex is never recomputed — only patched

So GraphDelta must befully explicit edge operations

## Dataclass definition

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional@dataclass(frozen=True)class GraphEdge:    source: str    target: str    relation: str  # e.g. wrp:depends_on, wrp:supersedes    weight: float = 1.0    metadata: Optional[dict] = None@dataclass(frozen=True)class GraphEdgeRemoval:    source: str    target: str    relation: str# ----------------------------# GraphDelta# ----------------------------@dataclassclass GraphDelta:    """    Incremental update to Kernel GraphIndex.    This avoids full recomputation of cross-plan graph state.    """    add_edges: List[GraphEdge] = field(default_factory=list)    remove_edges: List[GraphEdgeRemoval] = field(default_factory=list)    # Optional: nodes introduced or removed explicitly    add_nodes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    remove_nodes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # Origin tracking (important for debugging cross-plan causality)    source_plan_id: Optional[str] = None    batch_id: Optional[str] = None
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional@dataclass(frozen=True)class GraphEdge:    source: str    target: str    relation: str  # e.g. wrp:depends_on, wrp:supersedes    weight: float = 1.0    metadata: Optional[dict] = None@dataclass(frozen=True)class GraphEdgeRemoval:    source: str    target: str    relation: str# ----------------------------# GraphDelta# ----------------------------@dataclassclass GraphDelta:    """    Incremental update to Kernel GraphIndex.    This avoids full recomputation of cross-plan graph state.    """    add_edges: List[GraphEdge] = field(default_factory=list)    remove_edges: List[GraphEdgeRemoval] = field(default_factory=list)    # Optional: nodes introduced or removed explicitly    add_nodes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    remove_nodes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # Origin tracking (important for debugging cross-plan causality)    source_plan_id: Optional[str] = None    batch_id: Optional[str] = None
```

---

# 🧠 3. Design constraints (important invariants)

These are not optional — they define correctness.

---

## KernelDelta invariants

```
KD1: receipts must be append-onlyKD2: invalidations override inferenceKD3: affected_plans must include all touched PlanIdsKD4: delta must be replayable deterministically
```

```
KD1: receipts must be append-onlyKD2: invalidations override inferenceKD3: affected_plans must include all touched PlanIdsKD4: delta must be replayable deterministically
```

---

## GraphDelta invariants

```
GD1: add_edges and remove_edges are mutually exclusive per edge identityGD2: no implicit node creation from edges aloneGD3: edge identity = (source, target, relation)GD4: graph updates must be order-independent within a delta batch
```

```
GD1: add_edges and remove_edges are mutually exclusive per edge identityGD2: no implicit node creation from edges aloneGD3: edge identity = (source, target, relation)GD4: graph updates must be order-independent within a delta batch
```

---

# 🔁 4. How these two interact in KernelReduce

This is the important wiring:

```
def reduce_kernel(state: KernelState, delta: KernelDelta):    # 1. derive impacted plans    plans = resolve_affected_plans(delta)    # 2. rebuild or reuse PlanIR    plan_ir_updates = build_or_reuse_plan_ir(state, plans)    # 3. derive graph changes from plan diffs    graph_delta = build_graph_delta(plan_ir_updates)    # 4. apply graph delta incrementally    state.graph = apply_graph_delta(state.graph, graph_delta)    # 5. merge plan updates into kernel    state.plans.update(plan_ir_updates)    # 6. validate invariants    validate_kernel(state)    return state
```

```
def reduce_kernel(state: KernelState, delta: KernelDelta):    # 1. derive impacted plans    plans = resolve_affected_plans(delta)    # 2. rebuild or reuse PlanIR    plan_ir_updates = build_or_reuse_plan_ir(state, plans)    # 3. derive graph changes from plan diffs    graph_delta = build_graph_delta(plan_ir_updates)    # 4. apply graph delta incrementally    state.graph = apply_graph_delta(state.graph, graph_delta)    # 5. merge plan updates into kernel    state.plans.update(plan_ir_updates)    # 6. validate invariants    validate_kernel(state)    return state
```

---

# 🧩 5. Why this design works (important conceptual point)

This structure gives you three layers of separation:

---

## 1. Intent layer (KernelDelta)

> “Something changed”

“Something changed”

---

## 2. Structural layer (GraphDelta)

> “Relationships changed”

“Relationships changed”

---

## 3. Semantic layer (KernelState)

> “System meaning after reconciliation”

“System meaning after reconciliation”

---

# ⚡ 6. Upgrade path (so you don’t get stuck later)

These dataclasses are intentionally extensible toward:

### Future Kernel v2 additions:

```
- causal edges (not just structural edges)- weighted inference propagation- conflict resolution metadata- multi-authority identity resolution
```

```
- causal edges (not just structural edges)- weighted inference propagation- conflict resolution metadata- multi-authority identity resolution
```

If you reduce this entire design to its essence:

```
KernelDelta  = what changed in the worldGraphDelta   = what changed in relationshipsKernelState  = what the world becomes after reconciliation
```

Good — now we turn this into something you can actually run without it degenerating into a “clever reducer.”

What we’re building here is:

> astateful incremental kernel engine with deterministic pure steps + managed caches + explicit invalidation

astateful incremental kernel engine with deterministic pure steps + managed caches + explicit invalidation

I’ll define it in a way that fits your existing LOSM / WRP / conduit world, not a generic framework.

---

# 🧠 1. Core idea: KernelReduceEngine is NOT a function

It is:

> astate machine that orchestrates pure reducers

astate machine that orchestrates pure reducers

So instead of:

```
KernelState = reduce(KernelState, KernelDelta)
```

```
KernelState = reduce(KernelState, KernelDelta)
```

we now have:

```
KernelReduceEngine = orchestrator(    PlanReducer,    GraphReducer,    CacheManager,    Validator)
```

```
KernelReduceEngine = orchestrator(    PlanReducer,    GraphReducer,    CacheManager,    Validator)
```

---

# ⚙️ 2. Architecture overview

```
                +----------------------+KernelDelta --> |  Impact Analyzer     |                +----------+-----------+                           |                           v                +----------------------+                | PlanIR Cache Layer   |                +----------+-----------+                           |          +----------------+----------------+          |                                 |          v                                 v+----------------------+        +------------------------+| PlanIR Reducer      |        | Cache Reuse Layer      || (WRPProjection)     |        | (skip recompute)       |+----------+-----------+        +-----------+------------+           \                                /            \                              /             v                            v              +--------------------------+              | GraphDelta Builder       |              +-----------+--------------+                          |                          v              +--------------------------+              | GraphIndex Applier       |              +-----------+--------------+                          |                          v              +--------------------------+              | Kernel Validator         |              +--------------------------+
```

```
                +----------------------+KernelDelta --> |  Impact Analyzer     |                +----------+-----------+                           |                           v                +----------------------+                | PlanIR Cache Layer   |                +----------+-----------+                           |          +----------------+----------------+          |                                 |          v                                 v+----------------------+        +------------------------+| PlanIR Reducer      |        | Cache Reuse Layer      || (WRPProjection)     |        | (skip recompute)       |+----------+-----------+        +-----------+------------+           \                                /            \                              /             v                            v              +--------------------------+              | GraphDelta Builder       |              +-----------+--------------+                          |                          v              +--------------------------+              | GraphIndex Applier       |              +-----------+--------------+                          |                          v              +--------------------------+              | Kernel Validator         |              +--------------------------+
```

---

# 🧱 3. Core dataclass: KernelReduceEngine

This is the actual system controller.

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import Dict, Set, Optional, List@dataclassclass PlanCacheEntry:    plan_ir: object    receipt_hash: str    version: int@dataclassclass KernelReduceEngine:    """    Stateful incremental kernel execution engine.    Owns caching, invalidation, and orchestration.    """    # ----------------------------    # Persistent state    # ----------------------------    kernel_state: "KernelState"    plan_cache: Dict[str, PlanCacheEntry] = field(default_factory=dict)    # ----------------------------    # Execution metadata    # ----------------------------    version_counter: int = 0    # ----------------------------    # Public entrypoint    # ----------------------------    def reduce(self, delta: "KernelDelta") -> "KernelState":        """        Main entrypoint: apply incremental kernel update.        """        # 1. Determine impact scope        impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)        # 2. Invalidate caches        self._invalidate_cache(impact)        # 3. Rebuild or reuse PlanIRs        plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)        # 4. Build graph delta        graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(plan_ir_updates)        # 5. Apply graph update        self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)        # 6. Merge PlanIR updates        self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)        # 7. Validate kernel invariants        self._validate()        # 8. Commit version        self.version_counter += 1        self.kernel_state.version = self.version_counter        return self.kernel_state
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import Dict, Set, Optional, List@dataclassclass PlanCacheEntry:    plan_ir: object    receipt_hash: str    version: int@dataclassclass KernelReduceEngine:    """    Stateful incremental kernel execution engine.    Owns caching, invalidation, and orchestration.    """    # ----------------------------    # Persistent state    # ----------------------------    kernel_state: "KernelState"    plan_cache: Dict[str, PlanCacheEntry] = field(default_factory=dict)    # ----------------------------    # Execution metadata    # ----------------------------    version_counter: int = 0    # ----------------------------    # Public entrypoint    # ----------------------------    def reduce(self, delta: "KernelDelta") -> "KernelState":        """        Main entrypoint: apply incremental kernel update.        """        # 1. Determine impact scope        impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)        # 2. Invalidate caches        self._invalidate_cache(impact)        # 3. Rebuild or reuse PlanIRs        plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)        # 4. Build graph delta        graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(plan_ir_updates)        # 5. Apply graph update        self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)        # 6. Merge PlanIR updates        self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)        # 7. Validate kernel invariants        self._validate()        # 8. Commit version        self.version_counter += 1        self.kernel_state.version = self.version_counter        return self.kernel_state
```

---

# 🔍 4. Step-by-step internals

Now we define each stage properly.

---

## 4.1 Impact analysis (the MOST important optimization layer)

```
def _analyze_impact(self, delta: KernelDelta):    """    Determines minimal recomputation scope.    """    affected_plans = set(delta.affected_plans)    # Expand impact via cache + dependency graph    for plan_id in delta.affected_plans:        dependent_plans = self.kernel_state.globalGraph.get_dependents(plan_id)        affected_plans.update(dependent_plans)    return {        "plans": affected_plans,        "receipts": delta.receipts,        "invalidated": delta.invalidated_plans,    }
```

```
def _analyze_impact(self, delta: KernelDelta):    """    Determines minimal recomputation scope.    """    affected_plans = set(delta.affected_plans)    # Expand impact via cache + dependency graph    for plan_id in delta.affected_plans:        dependent_plans = self.kernel_state.globalGraph.get_dependents(plan_id)        affected_plans.update(dependent_plans)    return {        "plans": affected_plans,        "receipts": delta.receipts,        "invalidated": delta.invalidated_plans,    }
```

---

## 4.2 Cache invalidation (critical performance layer)

```
def _invalidate_cache(self, impact):    for plan_id in impact["plans"]:        if plan_id in self.plan_cache:            del self.plan_cache[plan_id]
```

```
def _invalidate_cache(self, impact):    for plan_id in impact["plans"]:        if plan_id in self.plan_cache:            del self.plan_cache[plan_id]
```

### Why this matters:

This is your “compiler cache busting” layer.

Without it:

- stale PlanIRs leak into kernel
stale PlanIRs leak into kernel

- cross-plan graph corruption appears
cross-plan graph corruption appears

---

## 4.3 PlanIR construction (WRP integration point)

```
def _build_plan_ir(self, impact, delta: KernelDelta):    updates = {}    for plan_id in impact["plans"]:        # reuse cache if possible        if plan_id in self.plan_cache:            updates[plan_id] = self.plan_cache[plan_id].plan_ir            continue        # otherwise rebuild using existing WRPProjectionBuilder        plan_ir = WRPProjectionBuilder.reduce(            plan_id=plan_id,            receipts=self._filter_receipts(plan_id, delta.receipts)        )        updates[plan_id] = plan_ir        # update cache        self.plan_cache[plan_id] = PlanCacheEntry(            plan_ir=plan_ir,            receipt_hash=self._hash_receipts(delta.receipts),            version=self.version_counter        )    return updates
```


---

## 4.4 GraphDelta construction

```
def _build_graph_delta(self, plan_ir_updates):    add_edges = []    remove_edges = []    for plan_id, plan_ir in plan_ir_updates.items():        for edge in plan_ir.crossRefs.added:            add_edges.append(edge)        for edge in plan_ir.crossRefs.removed:            remove_edges.append(edge)    return GraphDelta(        add_edges=add_edges,        remove_edges=remove_edges    )
```


---

## 4.5 Graph application (incremental core)

```
def _apply_graph_delta(self, graph_delta: GraphDelta):    graph = self.kernel_state.globalGraph    for edge in graph_delta.remove_edges:        graph.remove(edge)    for edge in graph_delta.add_edges:        graph.add(edge)
```

```

def _merge_plan_updates(self, plan_ir_updates):    for plan_id, plan_ir in plan_ir_updates.items():        self.kernel_state.plans[plan_id] = plan_ir
```

```
def _validate(self):    errors = []    # invariant checks    errors.extend(self.kernel_state.validate_no_dangling_edges())    errors.extend(self.kernel_state.validate_plan_consistency())    errors.extend(self.kernel_state.validate_cross_plan_rules())    if errors:        raise KernelValidationError(errors)
```

Good — now we’re at the layer that actually determines whether this system stays clean or turns into an inconsistent graph soup:

> Identity Resolution is the missing semantic spine between PlanIR and KernelState.

Identity Resolution is the missing semantic spine between PlanIR and KernelState.

Without it:

- cross-plan graphs lie silently
cross-plan graphs lie silently

- duplicates proliferate
duplicates proliferate

- “same thing” exists in multiple semantic universes
“same thing” exists in multiple semantic universes

- Kernel becomes structurally inconsistent even if every reducer is “correct”
Kernel becomes structurally inconsistent even if every reducer is “correct”

So we fix that properly.

---

# 🧠 1. What identity resolution actually is

It is NOT deduplication.

It is:

> acontinuity system for meaning across time, plans, and receipts

acontinuity system for meaning across time, plans, and receipts

So instead of:

- “this node equals that node”
“this node equals that node”

you get:

- “these nodes are manifestations of the same underlying identity over time”
“these nodes are manifestations of the same underlying identity over time”

---

# 🧬 2. Introduce KernelIdentityLayer

This sits between PlanIR and KernelState.

```
LOSMIR   ↓PlanIR (per-plan semantics)   ↓Identity Resolution Layer   ← NEW   ↓KernelState (global truth)
```

```
LOSMIR   ↓PlanIR (per-plan semantics)   ↓Identity Resolution Layer   ← NEW   ↓KernelState (global truth)
```

---

# 🧱 3. Core dataclasses

We’ll define three things:

- Identity
Identity

- IdentityMap
IdentityMap

- IdentityEvent (for evolution over time)
IdentityEvent (for evolution over time)

---

## 3.1 KernelIdentity

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional, Dict@dataclass(frozen=True)class IdentityId:    value: str@dataclassclass KernelIdentity:    """    A persistent semantic entity across PlanIRs.    This is NOT a node — it's the meaning behind nodes.    """    identity_id: IdentityId    # all known manifestations across plans    aliases: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # canonical representation (optional stabilized form)    canonical_node_id: Optional[str] = None    # provenance tracking    origin_plan_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # lifecycle state    status: str = "active"    # active | merged | deprecated | superseded    # version tracking    version: int = 0
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional, Dict@dataclass(frozen=True)class IdentityId:    value: str@dataclassclass KernelIdentity:    """    A persistent semantic entity across PlanIRs.    This is NOT a node — it's the meaning behind nodes.    """    identity_id: IdentityId    # all known manifestations across plans    aliases: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # canonical representation (optional stabilized form)    canonical_node_id: Optional[str] = None    # provenance tracking    origin_plan_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    # lifecycle state    status: str = "active"    # active | merged | deprecated | superseded    # version tracking    version: int = 0
```

---

## 3.2 IdentityMap (the core lookup structure)

```
@dataclassclass IdentityMap:    """    Global mapping from node-level artifacts → KernelIdentity.    """    node_to_identity: Dict[str, IdentityId] = field(default_factory=dict)    identity_store: Dict[str, KernelIdentity] = field(default_factory=dict)
```

```
@dataclassclass IdentityMap:    """    Global mapping from node-level artifacts → KernelIdentity.    """    node_to_identity: Dict[str, IdentityId] = field(default_factory=dict)    identity_store: Dict[str, KernelIdentity] = field(default_factory=dict)
```

---

## 3.3 IdentityEvent (this is your “semantic log of truth changes”)

```
@dataclassclass IdentityEvent:    """    Records how identities evolve over time.    """    event_type: str    # CREATE | MERGE | SPLIT | DEPRECATE | CANONICALIZE    source_identity: Optional[str] = None    target_identity: Optional[str] = None    node_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    reason: Optional[str] = None    timestamp: Optional[int] = None
```

```
@dataclassclass IdentityEvent:    """    Records how identities evolve over time.    """    event_type: str    # CREATE | MERGE | SPLIT | DEPRECATE | CANONICALIZE    source_identity: Optional[str] = None    target_identity: Optional[str] = None    node_ids: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)    reason: Optional[str] = None    timestamp: Optional[int] = None
```

# 🔁 4. Identity Resolution Engine

This is the operational component.

```
@dataclassclass IdentityResolutionEngine:    identity_map: IdentityMap    identity_events: List[IdentityEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
```

```
@dataclassclass IdentityResolutionEngine:    identity_map: IdentityMap    identity_events: List[IdentityEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
```

---

## 4.1 Core API: resolve identity for a node

```
def resolve(self, node_id: str, plan_context: str) -> IdentityId:    # existing mapping    if node_id in self.identity_map.node_to_identity:        return self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node_id]    # otherwise create new identity    identity = IdentityId(value=f"identity::{node_id}")    self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node_id] = identity.value    self.identity_map.identity_store[identity.value] = KernelIdentity(        identity_id=identity,        origin_plan_ids=[plan_context],        aliases=[node_id]    )    self.identity_events.append(IdentityEvent(        event_type="CREATE",        node_ids=[node_id],        reason="new unmapped node"    ))    return identity
```

```
def resolve(self, node_id: str, plan_context: str) -> IdentityId:    # existing mapping    if node_id in self.identity_map.node_to_identity:        return self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node_id]    # otherwise create new identity    identity = IdentityId(value=f"identity::{node_id}")    self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node_id] = identity.value    self.identity_map.identity_store[identity.value] = KernelIdentity(        identity_id=identity,        origin_plan_ids=[plan_context],        aliases=[node_id]    )    self.identity_events.append(IdentityEvent(        event_type="CREATE",        node_ids=[node_id],        reason="new unmapped node"    ))    return identity
```

---

# 🔗 5. Merge semantics (this is where systems usually break)

Identity merge is NOT deletion.

It isreconciliation of meaning.

```
def merge(self, id_a: str, id_b: str, reason: str):    if id_a == id_b:        return    a = self.identity_map.identity_store[id_a]    b = self.identity_map.identity_store[id_b]    # merge aliases    a.aliases.extend(b.aliases)    # unify origin tracking    a.origin_plan_ids.extend(b.origin_plan_ids)    # mark b as deprecated    b.status = "merged"    b.version += 1    # redirect node mappings    for node, idref in self.identity_map.node_to_identity.items():        if idref == id_b:            self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node] = id_a    self.identity_events.append(IdentityEvent(        event_type="MERGE",        source_identity=id_b,        target_identity=id_a,        reason=reason    ))
```

```
def merge(self, id_a: str, id_b: str, reason: str):    if id_a == id_b:        return    a = self.identity_map.identity_store[id_a]    b = self.identity_map.identity_store[id_b]    # merge aliases    a.aliases.extend(b.aliases)    # unify origin tracking    a.origin_plan_ids.extend(b.origin_plan_ids)    # mark b as deprecated    b.status = "merged"    b.version += 1    # redirect node mappings    for node, idref in self.identity_map.node_to_identity.items():        if idref == id_b:            self.identity_map.node_to_identity[node] = id_a    self.identity_events.append(IdentityEvent(        event_type="MERGE",        source_identity=id_b,        target_identity=id_a,        reason=reason    ))
```

---

# 🌐 6. How this plugs into KernelReduceEngine

This is the critical integration point.

During PlanIR → KernelState phase:

---

## Step 1: resolve all nodes

```
def resolve_plan_ir(self, plan_ir):    resolved_nodes = {}    for node in plan_ir.nodes:        identity = self.identity_engine.resolve(            node_id=node.id,            plan_context=plan_ir.planId        )        resolved_nodes[node.id] = identity    return resolved_nodes
```

```
def resolve_plan_ir(self, plan_ir):    resolved_nodes = {}    for node in plan_ir.nodes:        identity = self.identity_engine.resolve(            node_id=node.id,            plan_context=plan_ir.planId        )        resolved_nodes[node.id] = identity    return resolved_nodes
```

---

## Step 2: rewrite graph using identities

Instead of:

```
(plan A node 12) → depends_on → (plan B node 7)
```

```
(plan A node 12) → depends_on → (plan B node 7)
```

you get:

```
(identity 0xA) → depends_on → (identity 0xB)
```

```
(identity 0xA) → depends_on → (identity 0xB)
```

---

# 🧠 7. Why this is the missing layer

Without identity resolution:

- graph edges are syntactic
graph edges are syntactic

- PlanIRs are isolated semantic islands
PlanIRs are isolated semantic islands

- KernelState is just a union of projections
KernelState is just a union of projections

With identity resolution:

> Kernel becomes asingle semantic space with persistent entities

Kernel becomes asingle semantic space with persistent entities

---

# ⚡ 8. What you just unlocked architecturally

This enables:

### 1. Cross-plan continuity

Same concept across plans is unified.

### 2. Supersession chains

Old plan artifacts can be replaced cleanly.

### 3. Deduplication without loss

Nothing is deleted — only reinterpreted.

### 4. Causal lineage graphs

You can tracewhy an identity exists, not just that it exists.

---

# 🧩 9. The full stack now looks like this

```
LOSMIR  ↓PlanIR  ↓Identity Resolution Layer   ← YOU ARE HERE  ↓KernelState  ↓GraphIndex (identity-based)
```

```
LOSMIR  ↓PlanIR  ↓Identity Resolution Layer   ← YOU ARE HERE  ↓KernelState  ↓GraphIndex (identity-based)
```

# 🚨 10. The real consequence (this is the important part)

You are no longer building:

> a system of records

a system of records

You are building:

> asystem of persistent semantic entities evolving over time

asystem of persistent semantic entities evolving over time

Which means:

- state is no longer primary
state is no longer primary

- identity is primary
identity is primary

- state is just a projection of identity
state is just a projection of identity

# 🧠 1. Integration: IdentityResolution inside KernelReduceEngine

Right now your engine looks like:

```
KernelDelta → PlanIR → GraphDelta → KernelState
```

```
KernelDelta → PlanIR → GraphDelta → KernelState
```

We are inserting identity resolution as amandatory semantic rewrite layer between PlanIR and Graph construction.

---

## 🔧 Updated KernelReduceEngine (core wiring)

```
@dataclassclass KernelReduceEngine:    kernel_state: "KernelState"    plan_cache: Dict[str, PlanCacheEntry]    identity_engine: "IdentityResolutionEngine"    version_counter: int = 0
```

```
@dataclassclass KernelReduceEngine:    kernel_state: "KernelState"    plan_cache: Dict[str, PlanCacheEntry]    identity_engine: "IdentityResolutionEngine"    version_counter: int = 0
```

## 🧩 Updated reduce() flow

This is the new canonical pipeline:

```
def reduce(self, delta: "KernelDelta") -> "KernelState":    # 1. Impact analysis    impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)    # 2. Cache invalidation    self._invalidate_cache(impact)    # 3. PlanIR reconstruction    plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)    # 4. 🔥 IDENTITY RESOLUTION PHASE (NEW)    resolved_plan_ir = self._resolve_identities(plan_ir_updates)    # 5. Graph delta from resolved identities    graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(resolved_plan_ir)    # 6. Apply graph updates    self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)    # 7. Merge PlanIR    self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)    # 8. Validate kernel invariants    self._validate()    # 9. Commit version    self.version_counter += 1    self.kernel_state.version = self.version_counter    return self.kernel_state
```

```
def reduce(self, delta: "KernelDelta") -> "KernelState":    # 1. Impact analysis    impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)    # 2. Cache invalidation    self._invalidate_cache(impact)    # 3. PlanIR reconstruction    plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)    # 4. 🔥 IDENTITY RESOLUTION PHASE (NEW)    resolved_plan_ir = self._resolve_identities(plan_ir_updates)    # 5. Graph delta from resolved identities    graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(resolved_plan_ir)    # 6. Apply graph updates    self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)    # 7. Merge PlanIR    self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)    # 8. Validate kernel invariants    self._validate()    # 9. Commit version    self.version_counter += 1    self.kernel_state.version = self.version_counter    return self.kernel_state
```

## 🧠 Identity resolution hook

```
def _resolve_identities(self, plan_ir_updates):    resolved = {}    for plan_id, plan_ir in plan_ir_updates.items():        resolved_nodes = {}        for node in plan_ir.nodes:            identity = self.identity_engine.resolve(                node_id=node.id,                plan_context=plan_id            )            resolved_nodes[node.id] = identity        # rewrite PlanIR edges to identity space        plan_ir = self._rewrite_plan_ir_to_identities(            plan_ir,            resolved_nodes        )        resolved[plan_id] = plan_ir    return resolved
```

```
def _resolve_identities(self, plan_ir_updates):    resolved = {}    for plan_id, plan_ir in plan_ir_updates.items():        resolved_nodes = {}        for node in plan_ir.nodes:            identity = self.identity_engine.resolve(                node_id=node.id,                plan_context=plan_id            )            resolved_nodes[node.id] = identity        # rewrite PlanIR edges to identity space        plan_ir = self._rewrite_plan_ir_to_identities(            plan_ir,            resolved_nodes        )        resolved[plan_id] = plan_ir    return resolved
```

# ⚙️ 2. Full execution order (final engine semantics)

Now we formalize the entire system as a deterministic staged machine.

---

## 🧱 KernelReduce execution stages

```
STAGE 0: Receive KernelDeltaSTAGE 1: Impact Analysis  - compute affected plan set  - expand via dependency graphSTAGE 2: Cache Invalidation  - remove stale PlanIR entriesSTAGE 3: PlanIR Materialization  - WRPProjectionBuilder reduces receipts → PlanIRSTAGE 4: Identity Resolution  - map all PlanIR nodes → KernelIdentity  - rewrite PlanIR into identity-spaceSTAGE 5: GraphDelta Construction  - generate cross-plan edges (identity-level)STAGE 6: Graph Application  - incremental apply add/remove edgesSTAGE 7: Plan Merge  - update KernelState.plansSTAGE 8: Kernel Validation  - invariant checksSTAGE 9: Commit  - version bump  - snapshot optional
```

```
STAGE 0: Receive KernelDeltaSTAGE 1: Impact Analysis  - compute affected plan set  - expand via dependency graphSTAGE 2: Cache Invalidation  - remove stale PlanIR entriesSTAGE 3: PlanIR Materialization  - WRPProjectionBuilder reduces receipts → PlanIRSTAGE 4: Identity Resolution  - map all PlanIR nodes → KernelIdentity  - rewrite PlanIR into identity-spaceSTAGE 5: GraphDelta Construction  - generate cross-plan edges (identity-level)STAGE 6: Graph Application  - incremental apply add/remove edgesSTAGE 7: Plan Merge  - update KernelState.plansSTAGE 8: Kernel Validation  - invariant checksSTAGE 9: Commit  - version bump  - snapshot optional
```

---

## 🔒 Determinism rule

```
Same KernelState + same KernelDelta → identical KernelState'
```

```
Same KernelState + same KernelDelta → identical KernelState'
```

No hidden randomness, no implicit ordering dependence.

# ⚡ 3. Caching + invalidation semantics (this is where performance lives)

Now we formalize what actually gets reused.

## 🧱 Cache layers

You now effectively have3-tier cache hierarchy:

```
L1: PlanIR CacheL2: Identity CacheL3: GraphIndex Cache
```

```
L1: PlanIR CacheL2: Identity CacheL3: GraphIndex Cache
```

## 3.1 PlanIR cache rule

```
PlanCacheEntry:    plan_ir    receipt_hash    dependency_signature
```

```
PlanCacheEntry:    plan_ir    receipt_hash    dependency_signature
```

### Invalidation triggers:

- new receipts for plan
new receipts for plan

- identity merge affecting plan nodes
identity merge affecting plan nodes

- upstream dependency change
upstream dependency change

## 3.2 Identity cache rule

Identity resolution is stable unless:

- merge event occurs
merge event occurs

- split event occurs
split event occurs

- supersession event occurs
supersession event occurs

So:

```
Identity = append-only unless explicitly mutated
```

```
Identity = append-only unless explicitly mutated
```

---

## 3.3 Graph cache rule

GraphIndex is:

> strictly delta-applied, never rebuilt unless corruption detected

strictly delta-applied, never rebuilt unless corruption detected

Invalidation only happens on:

- invariant violation
invariant violation

- identity collapse event (major merge)
identity collapse event (major merge)

## 🧠 4. Dependency propagation model (critical glue)

This is what makes invalidation work correctly.

---

```
def propagate_invalidations(identity_events):    impacted_plans = set()    for event in identity_events:        if event.type == "MERGE":            impacted_plans.update(                self.identity_engine.get_plans_using(event.source_identity)            )    return impacted_plans
```

```
def propagate_invalidations(identity_events):    impacted_plans = set()    for event in identity_events:        if event.type == "MERGE":            impacted_plans.update(                self.identity_engine.get_plans_using(event.source_identity)            )    return impacted_plans
```

---

## Key idea

> Identity changes ripple downward into PlanIR invalidation

Identity changes ripple downward into PlanIR invalidation

This is what prevents stale semantic views.

# 🧠 1. What the Causal Lineage Engine actually is

At Kernel level, every artifact now has three meanings:

```
1. Structural: what it is (KernelState)2. Identity: what it refers to (Identity layer)3. Causal: why it exists (Lineage layer)
```

```
1. Structural: what it is (KernelState)2. Identity: what it refers to (Identity layer)3. Causal: why it exists (Lineage layer)
```

You now have:

- structure (GraphIndex)
structure (GraphIndex)

- identity (KernelIdentity)
identity (KernelIdentity)

- now: causality (LineageGraph)
now: causality (LineageGraph)

---

# 🧱 2. Core concept: Lineage is aderived graph of transformations

Not events.

Not logs.

Not history dumps.

It is:

> acompressed graph of semantic transformations between KernelStates

acompressed graph of semantic transformations between KernelStates

---

# 🧬 3. Data model: CausalLineageGraph

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set
```

---

## 3.1 LineageNode

Represents asemantic state change event, not raw input.

```
@dataclassclass LineageNode:    """    A single causal transformation in the Kernel.    """    node_id: str    type: str    # PLAN_REDUCE | IDENTITY_MERGE | GRAPH_UPDATE | INVALIDATION | SNAPSHOT    kernel_version: int    affected_plan_ids: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)    affected_identity_ids: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)    delta_hash: Optional[str] = None    timestamp: Optional[int] = None
```

```
@dataclassclass LineageNode:    """    A single causal transformation in the Kernel.    """    node_id: str    type: str    # PLAN_REDUCE | IDENTITY_MERGE | GRAPH_UPDATE | INVALIDATION | SNAPSHOT    kernel_version: int    affected_plan_ids: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)    affected_identity_ids: Set[str] = field(default_factory=set)    delta_hash: Optional[str] = None    timestamp: Optional[int] = None
```

---

## 3.2 LineageEdge

Represents causality between transformations.

```
@dataclassclass LineageEdge:    """    Causal dependency between kernel transformations.    """    source_node_id: str    target_node_id: str    relation: str    # CAUSED_BY | INVALIDATES | DERIVES_FROM | MERGES_INTO
```

```
@dataclassclass LineageEdge:    """    Causal dependency between kernel transformations.    """    source_node_id: str    target_node_id: str    relation: str    # CAUSED_BY | INVALIDATES | DERIVES_FROM | MERGES_INTO
```

---

## 3.3 CausalLineageGraph

```
@dataclassclass CausalLineageGraph:    nodes: Dict[str, LineageNode] = field(default_factory=dict)    edges: List[LineageEdge] = field(default_factory=list)    # reverse indices for fast queries    caused_by_index: Dict[str, Set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)    derived_index: Dict[str, Set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
```

```
@dataclassclass CausalLineageGraph:    nodes: Dict[str, LineageNode] = field(default_factory=dict)    edges: List[LineageEdge] = field(default_factory=list)    # reverse indices for fast queries    caused_by_index: Dict[str, Set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)    derived_index: Dict[str, Set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
```

---

# ⚙️ 4. Lineage Engine

This is the runtime component.

```
@dataclassclass LineageEngine:    graph: CausalLineageGraph
```

```
@dataclassclass LineageEngine:    graph: CausalLineageGraph
```

---

## 4.1 Record kernel step

Every KernelReduce cycle emits lineage.

```
def record_kernel_step(    self,    kernel_version: int,    step_type: str,    delta_hash: str,    affected_plans: set,    affected_identities: set) -> str:    node_id = f"ln:{kernel_version}:{step_type}"    node = LineageNode(        node_id=node_id,        type=step_type,        kernel_version=kernel_version,        affected_plan_ids=affected_plans,        affected_identity_ids=affected_identities,        delta_hash=delta_hash    )    self.graph.nodes[node_id] = node    return node_id
```

```
def record_kernel_step(    self,    kernel_version: int,    step_type: str,    delta_hash: str,    affected_plans: set,    affected_identities: set) -> str:    node_id = f"ln:{kernel_version}:{step_type}"    node = LineageNode(        node_id=node_id,        type=step_type,        kernel_version=kernel_version,        affected_plan_ids=affected_plans,        affected_identity_ids=affected_identities,        delta_hash=delta_hash    )    self.graph.nodes[node_id] = node    return node_id
```

---

## 4.2 Record causal relationship

```
def link(self, source: str, target: str, relation: str):    edge = LineageEdge(        source_node_id=source,        target_node_id=target,        relation=relation    )    self.graph.edges.append(edge)
```

```
def link(self, source: str, target: str, relation: str):    edge = LineageEdge(        source_node_id=source,        target_node_id=target,        relation=relation    )    self.graph.edges.append(edge)
```

---

# 🔁 5. Integration into KernelReduceEngine

Now we wire it into execution.

---

## Updated reduce() flow

```
def reduce(self, delta: KernelDelta):    # 1. Impact analysis    impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)    # 2. cache invalidation    self._invalidate_cache(impact)    # 3. PlanIR build    plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)    # 4. Identity resolution    resolved_plan_ir = self._resolve_identities(plan_ir_updates)    # 5. Graph delta    graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(resolved_plan_ir)    # 6. apply graph    self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)    # 7. merge plans    self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)    # 8. record lineage (NEW)    self._record_lineage(delta, impact, graph_delta)    # 9. validate    self._validate()    # 10. commit version    self.version_counter += 1    return self.kernel_state
```

```
def reduce(self, delta: KernelDelta):    # 1. Impact analysis    impact = self._analyze_impact(delta)    # 2. cache invalidation    self._invalidate_cache(impact)    # 3. PlanIR build    plan_ir_updates = self._build_plan_ir(impact, delta)    # 4. Identity resolution    resolved_plan_ir = self._resolve_identities(plan_ir_updates)    # 5. Graph delta    graph_delta = self._build_graph_delta(resolved_plan_ir)    # 6. apply graph    self._apply_graph_delta(graph_delta)    # 7. merge plans    self._merge_plan_updates(plan_ir_updates)    # 8. record lineage (NEW)    self._record_lineage(delta, impact, graph_delta)    # 9. validate    self._validate()    # 10. commit version    self.version_counter += 1    return self.kernel_state
```

---

## 5.1 Lineage recording hook

```
def _record_lineage(self, delta, impact, graph_delta):    step_id = self.lineage_engine.record_kernel_step(        kernel_version=self.version_counter,        step_type="KERNEL_REDUCE",        delta_hash=self._hash_delta(delta),        affected_plans=impact["plans"],        affected_identities=self.identity_engine.get_impacted_identities(delta)    )    # optional causal linking    self.lineage_engine.link(        source=step_id,        target=f"graph:{self.version_counter}",        relation="DERIVES_TO"    )
```

```
def _record_lineage(self, delta, impact, graph_delta):    step_id = self.lineage_engine.record_kernel_step(        kernel_version=self.version_counter,        step_type="KERNEL_REDUCE",        delta_hash=self._hash_delta(delta),        affected_plans=impact["plans"],        affected_identities=self.identity_engine.get_impacted_identities(delta)    )    # optional causal linking    self.lineage_engine.link(        source=step_id,        target=f"graph:{self.version_counter}",        relation="DERIVES_TO"    )
```

Good — but I’m going to tighten the framing a bit first, because otherwise this turns into three parallel systems that don’t agree on what “truth” means.At this point your architecture has converged on a single core idea:KernelState is not stored truth — it is a replayable projection of a semantic history graph.So the next three layers you asked for actually collapse into one spine:Semantic Replay Engine = “recompute alternative worlds”Conflict Resolution Policy = “what do we do when worlds disagree”Execution Context DAG mapping = “how this plugs into your LOSM runtime brain”We’ll build them in that order, but they will share the same invariants.🧠 1. Semantic Replay Engine (SRE)This is the “what if we replay history differently?” system.🔧 Core ideaInstead of:KernelState = latest(reduce(all deltas))You now support:KernelState' = reduce(deltas, policy=P)WhereP changes semantics of interpretation, not raw data.🧱 1.1 Replay configuration modelPythonRunfromdataclassesimportdataclass,fieldfromtypingimportList,Optional,Dict@dataclassclassReplayPolicy:"""Defines how Kernel history is replayed."""identity_resolution_mode:str="strict"# strict | permissive | historical | frozengraph_conflict_mode:str="fail_fast"# fail_fast | last_write_wins | merge | forklineage_reconstruction:bool=Trueallow_partial_kernel:bool=Falsetime_travel_mode:str="linear"# linear | branched | causal🧪 1.2 Replay EnginePythonRun@dataclassclassSemanticReplayEngine:base_kernel_state:"KernelState"lineage_graph:"CausalLineageGraph"defreplay(self,deltas:List["KernelDelta"],policy:ReplayPolicy) ->"KernelState":kernel=self._initialize_kernel(policy)fordeltaindeltas:kernel=self._apply_delta(kernel,delta,policy)returnkernel🔁 Key difference from normal reduceNormal engine:assumes identity engine is stableassumes graph rules are fixedReplay engine:treats identity + graph rules asparameters🧠 Why this mattersYou now support:“what if we didn’t merge these identities?”“what if we resolved cross-plan links differently?”“what if invalidations were strict instead of permissive?”This is yoursimulation layer, not production layer.⚖️ 2. Conflict Resolution SystemNow we define what happens when the kernel is inconsistent.This is where most systems collapse — because they pretend conflicts don’t exist.You will explicitly model them.🧱 2.1 Conflict typesPythonRunfromdataclassesimportdataclassfromtypingimportList,Optional@dataclassclassKernelConflict:conflict_id:strtype:str# IDENTITY_CONFLICT# GRAPH_CYCLE# PLAN_SUPERSESSION_AMBIGUITY# RECEIPT_DUPLICATIONaffected_nodes:List[str]severity:str# low | medium | high | criticaldescription:Optional[str]=None🧠 2.2 Conflict Resolution PolicyThis plugs into both KernelReduce and ReplayEngine.PythonRun@dataclassclassConflictPolicy:identity_conflict:str="merge"# merge | split | fail | defergraph_cycle:str="annotate"# annotate | break | failplan_supersession:str="latest_wins"receipt_duplication:str="idempotent_ignore"⚙️ 2.3 Resolver enginePythonRun@dataclassclassConflictResolver:policy:ConflictPolicydefresolve(self,conflicts:List[KernelConflict]) ->List[KernelConflict]:unresolved=[]forcinconflicts:ifc.type=="IDENTITY_CONFLICT":self._resolve_identity(c)elifc.type=="GRAPH_CYCLE":self._resolve_graph(c)else:unresolved.append(c)returnunresolved🧠 Key design shiftBefore:conflicts = errorsNow:conflicts = first-class semantic artifactsThey become:traceablereplayablepolicy-driven🌲 3. Execution Context DAG integration (your LOSM layer)Now we connect everything to your real system brain:LOSM Execution Context = causal + structural runtime graph🧱 3.1 Execution Context NodePythonRun@dataclassclassExecutionContextNode:node_id:strtype:str# KERNEL_DELTA# PLAN_REDUCE# IDENTITY_RESOLVE# GRAPH_APPLY# CONFLICT_RESOLVEinputs:List[str]=field(default_factory=list)outputs:List[str]=field(default_factory=list)kernel_version:Optional[int]=None🧱 3.2 Execution Context DAGPythonRun@dataclassclassExecutionContextDAG:nodes:Dict[str,ExecutionContextNode]edges:List[tuple]# (from_node, to_node, relation)🔁 3.3 How KernelReduce emits into Execution DAGEvery KernelReduce cycle becomes a DAG subgraph:PythonRundefemit_execution_context(kernel_delta,result):returnExecutionContextNode(node_id=f"exec:{kernel_delta.batch_id}",type="KERNEL_REDUCE",inputs=[kernel_delta.batch_id],outputs=[result.version])🧠 Why this mattersNow your system has:KernelState (truth)LineageGraph (why)Execution DAG (how)This completes the triangle:WHAT   → KernelStateWHY    → LineageGraphHOW    → ExecutionContextDAG🔗 4. Unification: how all three systems connectNow we unify everything:LOSMIR↓KernelDelta↓KernelReduceEngine↓KernelState↓├── Identity layer├── Graph layer├── Lineage layer↓ExecutionContextDAG (runtime trace)Replay system sits orthogonally:SemanticReplayEngine↳ uses LineageGraph + KernelDeltas↳ produces alternative KernelStatesConflict system sits in between:ConflictResolver↳ invoked during KernelReduce AND Replay🚨 5. The real architectural state you’ve reachedThis is no longer:event sourcinggraph processingor reduction systemsIt is:amulti-dimensional semantic execution runtime with replayable causality and policy-driven identity resolutionMore simply:You built:a system that canrecompute meaning, not just state🧭 If we go one step further (optional next move)There is one final layer that naturally emerges from this:👉 “Policy Compiler Layer”Where:ReplayPolicyConflictPolicyIdentityPolicybecome:versioned, type-checked configuration programsThat’s where this becomes asemantic operating system instead of a runtime engine.If you want to continue, that’s the real final boss layer.Sources

Good — but I’m going to tighten the framing a bit first, because otherwise this turns into three parallel systems that don’t agree on what “truth” means.

At this point your architecture has converged on a single core idea:

> KernelState is not stored truth — it is a replayable projection of a semantic history graph.

KernelState is not stored truth — it is a replayable projection of a semantic history graph.

So the next three layers you asked for actually collapse into one spine:

- Semantic Replay Engine = “recompute alternative worlds”
Semantic Replay Engine = “recompute alternative worlds”

- Conflict Resolution Policy = “what do we do when worlds disagree”
Conflict Resolution Policy = “what do we do when worlds disagree”

- Execution Context DAG mapping = “how this plugs into your LOSM runtime brain”
Execution Context DAG mapping = “how this plugs into your LOSM runtime brain”

We’ll build them in that order, but they will share the same invariants.

---

# 🧠 1. Semantic Replay Engine (SRE)

This is the “what if we replay history differently?” system.

---

## 🔧 Core idea

Instead of:

```
KernelState = latest(reduce(all deltas))
```

```
KernelState = latest(reduce(all deltas))
```

You now support:

```
KernelState' = reduce(deltas, policy=P)
```

```
KernelState' = reduce(deltas, policy=P)
```

WhereP changes semantics of interpretation, not raw data.

---

# 🧱 1.1 Replay configuration model

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional, Dict@dataclassclass ReplayPolicy:    """    Defines how Kernel history is replayed.    """    identity_resolution_mode: str = "strict"    # strict | permissive | historical | frozen    graph_conflict_mode: str = "fail_fast"    # fail_fast | last_write_wins | merge | fork    lineage_reconstruction: bool = True    allow_partial_kernel: bool = False    time_travel_mode: str = "linear"    # linear | branched | causal
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclass, fieldfrom typing import List, Optional, Dict@dataclassclass ReplayPolicy:    """    Defines how Kernel history is replayed.    """    identity_resolution_mode: str = "strict"    # strict | permissive | historical | frozen    graph_conflict_mode: str = "fail_fast"    # fail_fast | last_write_wins | merge | fork    lineage_reconstruction: bool = True    allow_partial_kernel: bool = False    time_travel_mode: str = "linear"    # linear | branched | causal
```

---

## 🧪 1.2 Replay Engine

```
@dataclassclass SemanticReplayEngine:    base_kernel_state: "KernelState"    lineage_graph: "CausalLineageGraph"    def replay(        self,        deltas: List["KernelDelta"],        policy: ReplayPolicy    ) -> "KernelState":        kernel = self._initialize_kernel(policy)        for delta in deltas:            kernel = self._apply_delta(kernel, delta, policy)        return kernel
```

```
@dataclassclass SemanticReplayEngine:    base_kernel_state: "KernelState"    lineage_graph: "CausalLineageGraph"    def replay(        self,        deltas: List["KernelDelta"],        policy: ReplayPolicy    ) -> "KernelState":        kernel = self._initialize_kernel(policy)        for delta in deltas:            kernel = self._apply_delta(kernel, delta, policy)        return kernel
```

---

## 🔁 Key difference from normal reduce

Normal engine:

- assumes identity engine is stable
assumes identity engine is stable

- assumes graph rules are fixed
assumes graph rules are fixed

Replay engine:

- treats identity + graph rules asparameters
treats identity + graph rules asparameters

---

## 🧠 Why this matters

You now support:

- “what if we didn’t merge these identities?”
“what if we didn’t merge these identities?”

- “what if we resolved cross-plan links differently?”
“what if we resolved cross-plan links differently?”

- “what if invalidations were strict instead of permissive?”
“what if invalidations were strict instead of permissive?”

This is yoursimulation layer, not production layer.

---

# ⚖️ 2. Conflict Resolution System

Now we define what happens when the kernel is inconsistent.

This is where most systems collapse — because they pretend conflicts don’t exist.

You will explicitly model them.

---

## 🧱 2.1 Conflict types

```
from dataclasses import dataclassfrom typing import List, Optional@dataclassclass KernelConflict:    conflict_id: str    type: str    # IDENTITY_CONFLICT    # GRAPH_CYCLE    # PLAN_SUPERSESSION_AMBIGUITY    # RECEIPT_DUPLICATION    affected_nodes: List[str]    severity: str    # low | medium | high | critical    description: Optional[str] = None
```

```
from dataclasses import dataclassfrom typing import List, Optional@dataclassclass KernelConflict:    conflict_id: str    type: str    # IDENTITY_CONFLICT    # GRAPH_CYCLE    # PLAN_SUPERSESSION_AMBIGUITY    # RECEIPT_DUPLICATION    affected_nodes: List[str]    severity: str    # low | medium | high | critical    description: Optional[str] = None
```

---

## 🧠 2.2 Conflict Resolution Policy

This plugs into both KernelReduce and ReplayEngine.

```
@dataclassclass ConflictPolicy:    identity_conflict: str = "merge"    # merge | split | fail | defer    graph_cycle: str = "annotate"    # annotate | break | fail    plan_supersession: str = "latest_wins"    receipt_duplication: str = "idempotent_ignore"
```

```
@dataclassclass ConflictPolicy:    identity_conflict: str = "merge"    # merge | split | fail | defer    graph_cycle: str = "annotate"    # annotate | break | fail    plan_supersession: str = "latest_wins"    receipt_duplication: str = "idempotent_ignore"
```

---

## ⚙️ 2.3 Resolver engine

```
@dataclassclass ConflictResolver:    policy: ConflictPolicy    def resolve(self, conflicts: List[KernelConflict]) -> List[KernelConflict]:        unresolved = []        for c in conflicts:            if c.type == "IDENTITY_CONFLICT":                self._resolve_identity(c)            elif c.type == "GRAPH_CYCLE":                self._resolve_graph(c)            else:                unresolved.append(c)        return unresolved
```

```
@dataclassclass ConflictResolver:    policy: ConflictPolicy    def resolve(self, conflicts: List[KernelConflict]) -> List[KernelConflict]:        unresolved = []        for c in conflicts:            if c.type == "IDENTITY_CONFLICT":                self._resolve_identity(c)            elif c.type == "GRAPH_CYCLE":                self._resolve_graph(c)            else:                unresolved.append(c)        return unresolved
```

---

## 🧠 Key design shift

Before:

> conflicts = errors

conflicts = errors

Now:

> conflicts = first-class semantic artifacts

conflicts = first-class semantic artifacts

They become:

- traceable
traceable

- replayable
replayable

- policy-driven
policy-driven
